name: Weight loss for chin definition

card.summary: Losing body fat to reveal the chin and jawline; plausible where fullness is soft tissue, but no studies test it and bone structure is not changed.
card.note: Wikipedia notes a double-chin look can also come from bone structure, not fat.

quick.overview:
Weight loss for chin definition is the idea that lowering overall body fat reduces fullness under the chin and makes the jawline look sharper.
Wikipedia describes a double chin as arising either from soft-tissue fat or from jaw bones that do not project far enough; no study found here tests weight loss for chin appearance.
quick.mechanism: Reducing overall body fat shrinks fat cells, including those under the chin. Whether fat loss can be targeted to one area is not established.
quick.risks: No risks specific to this approach are known. When the cause is bone structure, fat loss is not described as changing the chin's projection.

lead: Weight loss for chin definition is the approach of reducing overall body fat so that the area under the chin and along the jaw looks leaner and the chin and jawline stand out more. People use it to reduce a soft, rounded under-chin fold, often called a double chin, and to make the jaw outline sharper in photos and in person.[1]

Wikipedia describes two different causes of a double-chin look: in some overweight people, fat beneath the chin forms a fold, while in others, often of normal weight, the jaw bones do not project far enough forward so that the chin appears to blend into the neck.[1] Weight loss is relevant to the first type, and surgery such as genioplasty or jaw advancement is described for the second.[1][3]

Researchers at the University of Toronto digitally altered face photos and reported that a BMI change of about 1.33 kg/m2 was needed before people noticed a change in facial weight, and roughly twice that before faces looked more attractive.[4] A small study of gastric-bypass patients found modestly higher attractiveness ratings after about 20 percent weight loss.[5]

chain: Less subcutaneous fat under the chin and along the jaw
angle.text: People cut body fat through diet and exercise so that fullness under the chin and cheeks decreases and the jaw outline shows. Where the underlying bone is the limiting factor, individuals commonly combine fat loss with other approaches.

About 1.33 BMI points in one photo study[4]

paras: According to Wikipedia, the soft-tissue form is attributed to excess subcutaneous fat around the neck, whereas the bone form occurs in people of normal weight when the jaw bones are insufficiently projecting.[1] Subcutaneous fat is distributed unevenly through the body, with the number of fat cells varying by region and their size changing with nutritional state.[2] Because of this, how much leanness shows in the face varies by person.

A fully developed human skull has a chin of roughly 0.7 to 1.1 cm in projection, so small differences in bone and in overlying soft tissue can change how the chin reads from the side.[1] Wikipedia notes that fat distribution is largely genetic, with some regions, often the abdomen, losing fat more readily than others.[6]

sections.h: How weight loss affects the face
paras: In the Toronto photo study by Nicholas Rule and Daniel Re, published in Social Psychological and Personality Science, participants compared digitally altered faces; a BMI change of about 1.33 was needed to notice a difference in weight, and a decrease of about 2.38 (women) or 2.59 (men) before faces looked more attractive, equal to roughly 6.3 kg or 8.2 kg for average-height people.[4] Rule said people need to lose about twice as much for others to find them more attractive.[4] Because the faces were digitally altered, the figures come from simulated faces rather than people who lost weight.[4]

Exercise physiology literature addresses whether fat can be lost from one area by working the nearby muscle. Wikipedia's article on spot reduction reports that the scientific consensus among researchers is that it is not achievable, with fat lost from the body as a whole through diet and regular exercise.[6] It cites a study of tennis players in which the dominant forearm was larger from muscle but skinfold fat did not differ between arms, and a 2011 study of 24 sedentary adults who did seven abdominal exercises five days a week for six weeks and showed improved core endurance without a reduction in abdominal subcutaneous fat.[6]

For chin definition this means that people cutting body fat generally see the face and neck change as part of overall leaning out, and the timing and order in which areas lean varies between individuals.[6] Community members describe cutting for the jawline as a body-wide process in which the face becomes leaner at lower body-fat levels; this is how practitioners frame it, and no study has measured submental fat during a diet.[7]

Wikipedia lists surgical removal of the fat pad with a hyoid lift for the soft-tissue form and genioplasty or orthognathic surgery for bony deficiency.[1] Chin augmentation can be done by implants, sliding genioplasty or fillers.[3]

The Wikipedia double chin article also lists hyoid lift surgery (removing the fat pad and shortening jaw muscles), genioplasty alone for some patients with bony deficiency, orthognathic surgery to move one or both jaws forward, and maxillomandibular advancement for patients with sleep apnea.[1]

A 2015 Archives of Plastic Surgery study of 14 Roux-en-Y gastric bypass patients at Boston Medical Center, with mean weight loss of 20 percent, had online respondents rate before and after photos. Post-operative photos scored on average 0.256 points higher for attractiveness, while perceived age went up for six patients and down for five, and BMI change did not correlate significantly with either measure.[5] No study found tests lifestyle weight loss specifically for chin or jawline definition.

In looksmaxxing vocabulary, leaning out to show the jaw is often called cutting or leaning, and is discussed alongside jaw structure, since proponents say a jawline reads sharper once facial fat falls. T Nation training logs show members tracking cuts with meal plans and fasting windows, including intermittent fasting, as they work toward leaner bodies.[7][8] Wikipedia's fasting article notes that alternate-day fasting for two to six months is associated with reductions in body weight and BMI in overweight or obese adults, while evidence for sustained weight loss from fasting windows shorter than 24 hours is limited.[9]

The Toronto photo study's figures are sometimes used to illustrate how much change observers notice: roughly one BMI point before a weight change registers and about twice that before faces look more attractive.[4]

timeline.event: University of Toronto researchers report the BMI change needed for faces to look more attractive.[4]
Archives of Plastic Surgery study of facial photos before and after gastric bypass is published.[5]

lore.intro: Cutting for a sharper jaw is discussed on T Nation training logs as part of leaning out through diet, fasting windows and training.[7][8]

claims.claim: Cutting body fat reveals the jawline
claims.believers: Members logging a cut describe eating windows and calorie control as the path to a leaner look.[7]
claims.experts: Wikipedia describes soft-tissue double chins as arising from fat around the neck, and a Toronto photo study found a BMI change of about 1.33 was needed for people to notice facial weight change.[1][4]

claims.claim: Exercises can burn fat under the chin specifically
claims.believers: Spot-reduction ideas are commonly repeated in fitness circles.
claims.experts: Wikipedia reports that the scientific consensus is that spot reduction is not achievable, citing studies in which targeted training changed muscle but not local fat.[6]

claims.claim: Fat loss changes jaw bone structure
claims.believers: Some people expect that leaning out will give a more projecting chin.
claims.experts: Wikipedia describes bony chin deficiency in people of normal weight and lists genioplasty and orthognathic surgery for it.[1]
